Three groups: drop a vowel (podr-, sabr-, habr-, cabr-, querr-), insert a d (tendr-, pondr-, vendr-, saldr-, valdr-), two rogues (dir-, har-).

column1:
When and why do you use the
Futuro simple?
column2:
• Future events, formal or written register — el acto comenzará a las nueve. News, announcements, schedules.
  • Predictions — lloverá mañana.
  • Promises — te lo devolveré.
  • Conjecture about the present — ¿qué hora será?; estará en casa. The use you meet most in conversation — not about the future at all.
  • Emphatic commands — no matarás.
In speech, voy a hablar handles most near, planned futures. The simple future sounds more distant or formal.

column1:
Tricks and tips for the
Futuro simple
column2:
• The endings are the present tense of haber trimmed down (he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han). Historically the future was infinitive + haber fused — which is why the stem is the whole infinitive.
  • Accents on every form except nosotros.
  • Same twelve stems as the conditional.
  • Habrá = 'there will be', the future of hay.
